turn1.explanation: The unit fires most strongly on bird-name tokens, and it does so even when the word is a surname, band name, acronym or idiom (Swan, owls, Finch, Kestrel, lame duck, black/green swan, sparrow, Falcon, Flamingos, SWAN, Heron). A separate, weaker response sits on abbreviated month names that come right before a day number in dates (Sep, Oct., Nov., Aug., Feb., Sept.).
turn1.evidence: All 12 top examples peak on a bird word or its subword pieces, regardless of meaning (Robert Falcon Scott, Yvik Swan, an MRI 'SWAN sequence', 'lame duck'). Every mid-range example (5-7) is a news-style abbreviated month in a date, and I found no semantic or orthographic link to birds.
turn1.missing_data: Activations on full, unabbreviated month names and on non-bird animal names (e.g. 'Fox', 'Wolf' as surnames) would show whether the month response is a true second feature or a broader proper-noun effect.
